One-Off Pagani Utopia Is a Striking Work of Art With 24K Gold and Actual Moon Dust
13 photos
Photo: Instagram/varryx
Throw together a passion for cars and the financial ability to spend millions to satisfy that passion, and you have the perfect recipe for a striking car collection with one-off units that wouldn't even exist otherwise. That is exactly how Kris Singh's garage got started.
Kris Singh is a famous hypercar collector millionaire that probably doesn't even need an introduction with car enthusiasts. He loves fast and unique cars just about as much as he loves a good pun and customization projects that he can get actively involved in, so the newest addition to his collection is a sum of all these things.
It's a Pagani Utopia with a unique and inimitable paintjob and an outrageous interior that strives to match it and do it justice. Singh calls it La Madonna of the Car Nation, an excellent pun on Leonardo's famous 15th century painting Madonna of the Carnation because this exact shade of gold that was used for the car is inspired by the one Leonardo used.
Singh took delivery of the vehicle just a few days ago, at the 2026 Pagani Raduno Vanishing Point event that took place in Sicily, Italy, and obviously turned the moment into a viral video. Noticeably proud and beyond ecstatic, he made sure to take his fans and followers along for the ride (heh!), giving them a glimpse at a vehicle that had been – quite literally – eight years in the making.
Photo: Instagram/sparky18888 It's not that painting the Utopia and customizing its interior took that long, but rather that Singh's idea took this long to take root. It first sprung to his mind in early 2018, when he bought a piece of rock from the Moon and he assumed that grinding it and using it as base for a custom paint would be the ultimate flex in car customization.
He wasn't wrong.
Later that year, Singh announced that he would be working with Karosserie to develop a custom paint called Karosserie Lunar Red, inspired by the iconic red sole of the Louboutin shoes and containing ground Lunar dust, for a new Aston Martin Valkyrie. By 2024, the plan fell through, seemingly because Aston Martin couldn't keep their end of the deal, or so Singh would end up saying on his social media.
Photo: Instagram/varryx Disappointed, he turned to Pagani, having already been a loyal customer for years. The paint that should have been used for the Valkyrie would go on a Utopia, and he would still become the first person to own a car painted with actual Moon dust.
Sometime down the road, the Karosserie Lunar Red became Karosserie Lunar Gold, as shown in the videos at the bottom of the page and the photos in the gallery. It's made with the ground Lunar rock and 24K gold bar shavings, and while it might look like a regular pearly/sparkly gold to the untrained eye, it's probably different if you can see it in person.
The interior matches the exterior in outrageousness, with black leather, gold stitching, and 24K gold covered elements throughout. It's more high fashion with a dash of divisiveness than space-inspired, leaning towards the opulence and maximalism of the House of Versace than the utilitarianism of space design or the classical beauty of the Leonardo painting.
Photo: Instagram/varryx Singh himself highlights the seven-speed gear shifter, the pedals, and the rims of the gauges on the dashboard, all of which are covered in 24K gold. The patterned gold and black leather seats are elaborate and vibrant, with a design that received input from Singh's partner, also shown in the video.
The 6.0-liter twin-turbo Mercedes- AMG V12 engine was put together and branded by Spark 18888 aka The King aka Rober Beit, a prominent hypercar collector and asset manager from Connecticut, and a good friend of Singh's. Millionaires always hang in tight circles, but hypercar collector millionaires even more so.
Of the 229 Pagani Utopias produced, only 99 are coupes, with one selling for about $2.5 million. Singh's is clearly much more valuable now, if only for its unique paintjob and the amount of gold used for customizing it. This much gold can't possibly be to everyone's tastes, but there's no denying the artistry and the hard work behind it.
Photo: Instagram/varryx The Madonna of the Car Nation joins a collection that includes a Pagani Huayra BC dubbed Macchina Volante, a Huayra La Monza Lisa, which happens to be the most driven Pagani in existence, a 1-of-5 Zonda Cinque, and a Veyron Grand Sport Vitesse formerly owned by Arnold Schwarzenegger.
Singh also owns several Bugattis, four Chirons, several Ferraris, Rolls-Royces, Lamborghinis, and Hummers .
Photo: Instagram/varryx Singh is said to be worth an estimated $200 million, so he clearly doesn't lack the funds to turn even his wildest dreams into (car) reality. Even if that takes eight long years, a public spat with Aston Martin, a piece of rock from the Moon, and whatever effort and money went into turning this Utopia into this sparkly, eye-catching piece of art.
